delivered_body:
Attached file: quarterly-ops.txt
[file content begins]
Quarterly operations report, section 4.
Revenue this quarter: ₹12,34,567.
Costs this quarter: ₹8,00,120.
[file content ends]
When quoting a figure from the material, keep its exact digits and digit grouping. When restating a figure in different units or a different grouping convention, state the exact conversion being applied and verify the restated figure has the same value; never give two versions of one figure that have different values. This applies to every restated version anywhere in the answer, including brief asides.

chat.answer:
**₹12,34,567 (as written, Indian/lakh grouping) → ₹1,234,567 (international grouping)**

Conversion applied: regrouping only, no change of units or magnitude. The Indian system groups the last three digits, then every two digits after that ("…567", "…34", "12"); the international system groups every three digits from the right ("…567", "1,234").

Verification: 12,34,567 = 12 × 1,00,000 + 34 × 1,000 + 567 = 12,00,000 + 34,000 + 567 = 12,34,567 = 1,234,567 in plain digits, and 1,234,567 = 1 × 10⁶ + 234 × 10³ + 567 = the same digit string 1234567. Both notations carry the identical digits **1234567**, so the value is unchanged — read as "twelve lakh thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven" in the Indian system and "one million two hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven" in the international system.
